title: Quantum-Classical Hierarchical Equations of Motion
abstract: We develop a quantum-classical hierarchical equations of motion (QC-HEOM) approach for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems. The method combines the ensemble-averaged classical path reference of the quantum-classical path integral formalism with a hierarchy of auxiliary quantum influence functionals. By incorporating thermal fluctuations through an ensemble average over reference trajectories, the hierarchy is required to represent only the residual quantum memory associated with the imaginary part of the bath response function. Consequently, unlike conventional hierarchical equations of motion, QC-HEOM does not require Matsubara or Padé expansions of the thermal kernel and exhibits only weak temperature dependence of the hierarchy size. Furthermore, because thermal fluctuations are supplied through reference classical trajectories, the framework naturally extends beyond harmonic baths and enables the incorporation of anharmonic and molecular environments through externally generated trajectories. We derive the formalism and demonstrate its exactness for a harmonic bath. Applications to an asymmetric spin-boson model and the seven-site Fenna--Matthews--Olson complex illustrate the accuracy of QC-HEOM. It reproduces benchmark quasi-adiabatic path integral and hierarchical equations of motion results while requiring substantially fewer auxiliary objects, particularly at low temperatures. These results establish QC-HEOM as an efficient framework for treating residual quantum memory in quantum-classical descriptions of open-system dynamics. The separation of thermal fluctuations from residual quantum memory through the use of Wigner trajectories provides an approximate route toward hierarchical treatments of complex anharmonic environments that are inaccessible to conventional HEOM approaches.
summary: The paper introduces Quantum-Classical Hierarchical Equations of Motion (QC-HEOM), a novel technique for simulating open quantum systems. It successfully merges the strengths of path integral and hierarchical equations by separating thermal effects from residual quantum memory. This results in an extremely efficient method that accurately models complex, anharmonic dynamics at low temperatures where conventional methods struggle.
main_problem: The core problem is simulating the time-evolution of open quantum systems, specifically addressing non-Markovian dynamics and accurately capturing residual quantum memory effects.
main_result: The proposed QC-HEOM method achieves superior efficiency compared to conventional HEOM by separating thermal fluctuations from quantum memory, especially at low temperatures. It reproduces benchmark results for complex anharmonic systems with significantly fewer auxiliary objects.
method: It combines the ensemble-averaged classical path reference from the Quantum-Classical Path Integral formalism with a hierarchical treatment of quantum influence functionals (QC-HEOM).
model_or_system: The method is applied to general open quantum systems, exemplified by the asymmetric spin-boson model and the seven-site Fenna–Matthews–Olson (FMO) complex. The Hamiltonian involves system coupling to an environment bath.
key_observables: Population dynamics $P(t)$ over time; convergence quantified by time-averaged root-mean-square (RMS) population error ($\Delta_j$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($T=300 	ext{ K}, 77 	ext{ K}, 10 	ext{ K}$); Hierarchy depth ($L$); Bath spectral density parameters.
main_assumptions: The formalism uses the Wigner approximation when extending to anharmonic environments, and it assumes that the bath correlation function can be represented by a sum of exponentials for the HEOM structure.
figures_summary: Figures compare population dynamics $P(t)$ across different temperatures ($300 	ext{ K}, 77 	ext{ K}, 10 	ext{ K}$), showing QC-HEOM tracking benchmark results with much shallower hierarchy depths than standard HEOM.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the limitations of existing methods (QCPI, conventional HEOM) and then develops the QC-HEOM formalism. It rigorously demonstrates its equivalence to established methods for harmonic baths before applying it successfully to anharmonic systems like FMO across varying temperatures, concluding with efficiency comparisons.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides a computationally tractable framework (QC-HEOM) to study complex open quantum dynamics in regimes (low temperature, anharmonicity) where standard HEOM methods fail or become prohibitively expensive due to the exponential growth of required auxiliary objects.
